job_description: Context: Mukti Cox`s Bazar has been awarded direct funding from UNOCHA through the Bangladesh Humanitarian Fund (BHF) to implement a 9-month project titled “ Locally-Led GBV Response and Prevention: Enhancing Access to Life-Saving GBV Services and Risk Mitigation through Women and Girls Safe Spaces in Cox’s Bazar and Bhasan Char”  from January to September 2027. The project aims to improve access to safe, confidential, and survivor-centered Gender-Based Violence (GBV) services for Rohingya women and girls while strengthening community-based prevention and risk mitigation mechanisms. The project will contribute to operate 14 Women Friendly Spaces (WFS) across Rohingya camps and Bhasan Char and it will provide GBV case management, psychosocial support, referrals, dignity kit distribution, awareness sessions, safety audits, and community engagement activities. The intervention is expected to directly reach 27,500 refugees, particularly women, girls, persons with disabilities, and other vulnerable groups. By promoting locally-led humanitarian action, strengthening community structures, and enhancing coordination with relevant stakeholders, the project will contribute to safer and more protective environments for women and girls in the Rohingya response. Job Summary:  MHPSS Officer will be based at the Project Office in Ukhiya/Teknaf, with frequent travel to targeted camps. She will provide technical supervision and quality assurance for mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS) interventions. Responsibilities will also include delivering structured and non-structured psychosocial support (PSS), building the capacity of Case Workers to conduct PSS sessions inside Women Friendly Spaces (WFS) and supporting Community Mobilizers in outreach PSS sessions and Psychological First Aid (PFA). The role contributes to ensuring that the GBV team delivers services in line with the IASC Guidelines on Mental Health and Psychosocial Support in Emergency Settings. This position is open to female candidates only. She will work under the direct supervision of the Project Manager and Technical Supervision of MHPSS Specialist of Mukti Cox’s Bazar. Job responsibilities: Technical supervision and quality assurance of MHPSS interventions :   Provide technical supervision and quality assurance for MHPSS interventions across the targeted camps and WFS, in line with the IASC MHPSS Guidelines and survivor-centered principles. Assess current PSS interventions and the knowledge and skills of staff in the WFS, and identify gaps and needs. Develop and implement training, mentoring and supervision plans that equip Case Workers and Case Managers to deliver PSS and apply psychosocial support tools. Conduct regular field visits, observe PSS sessions, and provide feedback and on-the-job coaching to field staff. Ensure quality, confidentiality and safe referral in PSS delivery, and refer cases that need specialized mental health care to appropriate service providers. Support the development, adaptation and field-testing of PSS manuals, guidance and IEC materials. Contribute to project planning and ensure that MHPSS activities are delivered as scheduled. Direct delivery of psychosocial support : Deliver structured and non-structured PSS sessions for women and adolescent girls, including survivors, inside the WFS. Provide Psychological First Aid (PFA) and conduct individual and group PSS as per need. Support Community Mobilizers in conducting outreach PSS sessions and PFA in the community. Provide technical guidance to Case Workers on complex cases through case discussions. Ensure that persons with disabilities, adolescent girls and other at-risk groups are included in PSS activities. Capacity building and staff care: Build the capacity of Case Workers to conduct PSS sessions inside the WFS through regular trainings, coaching and mentoring. Organizational Context & Operational Rationale;  Nari Maitree (NM) is a distinguished, national women-led non-governmental organization with 43 years of committed service dedicated to advancing women`s empowerment, gender justice, human rights, child protection, and community resilience across Bangladesh. Under the multi-year humanitarian initiative "Protection-Centred and Locally Driven Response for Rohingya Refugees in Cox’s Bazar", funded by the Australian Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade (DFAT) in consortium partnership with the International Rescue Committee (IRC) and other national partners, Nari Maitree leads the consortium’s specialized thematic implementation on Gender-Based Violence (GBV) Prevention & Response and Gender Equality, Disability, and Social Inclusion (GEDSI). Beginning 01 January 2027, IRC will execute a structured, phased handover transferring full operational and technical management of direct Protection Case Management and Primary Health Care Centre (PHC) case management services to Nari Maitree. To ensure rigorous case management, supervision of frontline caseworkers, and compliance with the Bangladesh Protection Sector Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), Nari Maitree is recruiting 05 (Five) dedicated Protection Case Management Officers for a 24-month tenure (January 2027 to December 2028). 2. Position Summary:  The Protection Case Management Officer (PCMO) will be responsible for the day-to-day coordination, execution, and technical quality of Protection Case Management (PCM) and Individual Protection Assistance (IPA) services within assigned Rohingya refugee camps. Duty Station:  Ukhiya, Cox`s Bazar, Bangladesh (with frequent field visits to Rohingya camps and host communities) Reports To:  Project Coordinator Type of Contract:  Fixed-Term (Project Duration) Position Summary:  The Case Management Supervisor will oversee the quality, safety, and survivor-centered delivery of Gender-Based Violence (GBV) case management services in designated Rohingya camps and host communities. The incumbent will provide direct technical guidance to Case Workers, ensure compliance with international GBV standards and survivor-centered approaches, and manage data entry, security, and trend analysis using the Violence Against Women and Girls Information Management System (VAWGIMS) / GBVIMS. This role actively embeds Nari Maitree’s leadership in gender diversity and intersectionality by ensuring case management services are accessible, safe, and inclusive for all women, girls, and gender-diverse individuals. Assignment Duration:  Tentative 24 months Key Responsibilities & Essential Functions 1. Technical Supervision & Case Management Quality Assurance Supervise, mentor, and build the capacity of GBV Case Workers to ensure case management aligns with survivor-centered principles, Inter-Agency Case Management Guideline, and IRC-harmonized protection standards. Review case files and documentation using GBV Incident Tracker regularly to assess the quality, completeness, and timeliness of case management interventions, and provide constructive feedback to Case Workers for improvement. Provide technical guidance to Case Workers on risk assessment, safety planning, prioritization of cases, and appropriate decision-making for cases involving heightened protection risks or complex needs. Conduct regular case reviews, case conferences, and one-on-one supervision sessions to address complex cases, ensuring proper assessment, safety planning, and referral based on the survivor`s informed consent . Provide structured supervision to Case Workers using prescribed Case Management supervision tools and identify capacity-building needs to develop and implement appropriate learning and capacity-building plans through the supervision process.Document key supervision findings, agreed actions, and follow-up points using prescribed supervision tools and ensure that identified actions are followed through within agreed timelines. Ensure appropriate and timely case closure in line with the Inter-Agency Case Management Guideline and oversee Client Satisfaction Surveys for closed cases, using findings to improve the quality and survivor-centeredness of Case Management services. Lead and guide the implementation of the Women Rise Structured PSS curriculum, ensuring proper pre-screening, feedback and fidelity to improve implementation quality, and facilitation of FGDs using the prescribed Women Rise tools. Lead and support safety audits conducted by IRC as a representative of Nari Maitree, ensuring quality data collection through FGDs and KIIs across Nari Maitree-implemented locations. Guarantee that services are fully inclusive and safe for vulnerable populations, including adolescent girls, women with disabilities (in coordination with CDD), and gender-diverse individuals. 2. Information Management & GBVIMS Oversight Oversee the safe, confidential, and ethical collection, storage, and management of GBV case data using GBVIMS. Analyze monthly case management data to identify trends, gaps in referral pathways, and emerging protection risks without compromising client confidentiality. Prepare and submit monthly Case Management, Unstructured PSS, Case Closure, and Client Satisfaction reports within established deadlines, ensuring the accuracy and validation of reported data. Ensure proper implementation of Women Rise MEAL tools and timely submission of data through the CommCare platform.Prepare monthly, quarterly, and annual disaggregated case management statistics and qualitative insights for consortium reporting and technical review within the GEDSI CoP. 3. Sector Coordination & Referral Pathways Map and regularly update functional, multi-sectoral referral pathways (health, legal, MHPSS, safe shelter, WASH, and food security) in assigned operational areas. Represent Nari Maitree at camp-level GBV Sub-Sector working groups, case management coordination meetings, and discussions with Camp-in-Charge (CiC) officials and Site Management. Represent Nari Maitree in the GBV Sub-Sector, GBV Case Management Working Group, GBVIMS Task Team, and other relevant sector-level coordination and technical working groups.Coordinate closely with consortium partners (IRC for health/protection, CDD for disability inclusion, BTS for child protection) to streamline multi-disciplinary support for survivors. 4. Community Mobilization & Safe Spaces Management Oversee the operational quality and safety of Nari Maitree’s Women and Girls Safe Spaces (WGSS) or community response points. Support community-level awareness and prevention activities, ensuring community engagement initiatives link survivors safely to confidential support services. Establish, facilitate, and provide technical guidance to adolescent steering committees and community-based groups to strengthen meaningful participation, leadership, and community ownership. Facilitate coordination between WGSS, adolescent steering committees, community-based groups, and relevant service providers to strengthen safe referral pathways and community-level support. 5. Safeguarding, PSEAH & Ethics Strict enforcement of zero-tolerance policies regarding Protection from Sexual Exploitation, Abuse, and Harassment (PSEAH), Child Safeguarding, and data breaches. Ensure all case management staff strictly adhere to ethical guidelines, informed consent protocols, and client confidentiality.
